research_question: What is the effect of oral hygiene, diet, and feeding practice advice, compared with standard care, on caries presence in any primary teeth in young children?
treatment_label: oral hygiene, diet, and feeding practice advice
outcome_description: Presence of dental caries in any primary teeth (measured across diagnostic thresholds such as dmfs, d2, d3mft, or white spot lesions at ages 1 to 6 years)
positive_direction: Lower risk of caries presence in any primary teeth, favoring the oral hygiene, diet, and feeding practice advice intervention over standard care
search_queries: oral hygiene diet feeding advice caries young children trial
feeding practice oral health education caries primary teeth randomized controlled trial
dietary feeding advice dental caries preschool children controlled study
inclusion_criteria: Controlled trials evaluating oral hygiene, diet, or feeding practice advice delivered to parents, caregivers, or young children compared to standard care or inactive control.
Studies reporting quantitative data on caries presence in any primary teeth in children up to age 6 years across diagnostic criteria (e.g., dmfs, d2, d3mft, or white spot lesions).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (e.g., systematic reviews, meta-analyses, study protocols, editorials, or commentaries).
No comparison between an oral health advice intervention and a standard care or control condition.
No extractable quantitative outcome data on caries presence or incidence in primary teeth (e.g., dichotomous event counts per arm, risk ratios, or odds ratios).
Unrelated to oral health/feeding advice interventions or pediatric dental caries.
moderators_to_extract: caries diagnostic threshold (e.g., enamel/white spot vs dentinal cavitation)
child age at final outcome assessment / length of follow-up
intervention components (diet/feeding practice advice, oral hygiene instruction, or combined)
delivery setting and format (e.g., home visits, primary care clinics, group education)
background fluoridation status of the study population
effect_size_note: Risk Ratio (RR) pooled using the number of children with caries presence in any primary teeth and the total number of children analyzed/randomized per arm.
